newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Voting starts in Bulgarian presidential run-off.
newsitem.headline: Voting starts in Bulgarian presidential run-off.

text.p: Voting started on Sunday in Bulgaria's presidential election run-off between opposition candidate Petar Stoyanov and Culture Minister Ivan Marazov, the candidate of the governing Socialists.
Opinion polls predict a comfortable win for Stoyanov, a 44-year-old lawyer who beat incumbent president Zhelyu Zhelev in a U.S.-style primary election in June.
Marazov lagged 17 points behind Stoyanov in last Sunday's first round but many votes went to protest candidates.
The turnout on Sunday is expected to be lower than last week's 63 percent.
Polls close at 7 p.m. (1700 GMT) and first projections by polling agencies are expected about an hour later.
The election coincides with a visit by an International Monetary Fund mission discussing terms for release of a $115-million credit which is vital to prevent Bulgaria defaulting on its foreign debt.
The head of the mission, Anne McGuirk, is due to meet Prime Minister Zhan Videnov later on Sunday.
